os-efcore-postgres.title: PostgreSQL
os-efcore-postgres.summary: PostgreSQL through Npgsql with a safe setup: SSL required, Npgsql's own retries, dates turned to UTC for `timestamptz`, and its error codes turned into clear results.

gives.1: SSL is required whatever the connection string says, and full certificate checking is one switch away.
gives.2: Temporary failures are retried by Npgsql's own strategy, and `TranAsync` stays safe under it.
gives.3: Any `DateTimeOffset` is turned to UTC before it is written, so `timestamptz` never rejects a value.

connection.title: Connecting safely
connection.summary: Give a connection string; SSL, retries and UTC dates are set for you.

1.title: Core registration
1.text: `AddOSPostgres` passes your string to `UseNpgsql`; nothing else to set up.

2.title: SSL by options
2.text: The options decide the SSL mode, not the string.

3.title: UTC only
3.text: `timestamptz` accepts only UTC, so every date is converted.

1.title: Registering
1.text: `AddOSPostgres` registers your context through the core and passes your connection string to `UseNpgsql`. From EF Core 9 on, Npgsql builds and caches its connection source itself, so there is nothing else to set up.

2.title: SSL mode
2.text:
The options always decide the SSL mode, whatever the string says.

`Require` by default (encrypted), `VerifyFull` when you set `VerifyServerCertificate` (encrypted and the server's certificate and name are checked), and `Prefer` only when you set `Encrypt = false` for development.

3.title: Retry, dates, names
3.text:
With `RetryOnFailure` on, temporary failures are retried by Npgsql's strategy using `RetryCount` and `RetryDelay` from `EFCoreOptions`.

PostgreSQL's `timestamptz` accepts only UTC, so every `DateTimeOffset` is turned to UTC before writing and comes back as UTC.

Lower-case snake_case names are the custom on PostgreSQL: call `ApplySnakeCaseName()` in `OnModelCreating`, but only for a new database.

4.title: Concurrent edits
4.text: Edits by two people are caught by the core `Version` token, not `xmin`, so one model works on every database.

secure.title: What the connection really uses
secure.note: The string asked for no SSL; the options made it `Require`.

snake-case.title: snake_case names for PostgreSQL
snake-case.note: Call it last in `OnModelCreating`, on a new database only.

type.PostgresOptions: The connection string and the security and retry switches.

PostgresOptions.VerifyServerCertificate: Also checks the server's certificate and host name (`VerifyFull`). Off by default; turn it on when the server has a proper certificate.

PostgresEx.AddOSPostgres: Registers a context on PostgreSQL. Registers OS.EFCore too when it is not registered yet, so one call is enough; call `AddOSEFCore` as well, before or after, only to change its settings.
PostgresEx.UseOSPostgres: Applies the PostgreSQL setup to a builder.

errors.title: Errors and what was tested
errors.summary: How PostgreSQL errors turn into results, and an honest note on testing.

1.title: SQLSTATE codes
1.text: Errors arrive as five-character SQLSTATE codes that map to `data.*`.

3.title: No leaks
3.text: Host and database names never reach a result.

4.title: Honest note
4.text: Only unit tests so far; no real PostgreSQL server yet.

1.title: Recognized codes
1.text:
PostgreSQL reports errors with a five-character SQLSTATE code. These are recognized (checked against the PostgreSQL documentation): 23505 gives `data.duplicate` with the constraint, 23502 gives `data.required` with the column, 23503 gives `data.missingRef` (or `data.inUse` when deleting), 22001 gives `data.tooLong`.

40001 (serialization failure), 40P01 (deadlock), 55P03 (lock not available) and 57014 (query canceled) give `data.busy`. 57P01, 57P02, 57P03, 53300 and every code that starts with 08 give `data.offline`.

2.title: Other errors
2.text:
A timeout on the client side is `data.busy`, any other Npgsql connection error is `data.offline`, and anything else is `data.error`.

Field and constraint names come from the exception's own fields; host and database names never reach a result.

3.title: Honest note
3.text:
This package has been tested only with unit tests, using real PostgreSQL exceptions built with Npgsql's public constructor.

It has not yet run against a real PostgreSQL server; do that before you rely on it in production.

save-item.title: Turn a PostgreSQL result into a message
save-item.note: A serialization failure that did not clear after retries arrives as `data.busy`.
